title: The ambient surface reports AtRest without anything ever reading the router
found: 2026-09-02, recorded while fixing DEF-101
evidence: AmbientSurfaceModel.State initialises to AmbientRouterState.AtRest and UpdateState is called by nothing in the build. AmbientFlyoutView therefore renders 'Router ready' and 'All systems quiet. No active calls or queued items.' whatever the router is doing, including when it is not running. AmbientPresentation.TrayToolTip formats the same state into 'MCP Router - Ready'.
why-it-matters: It is a claim about the router made by a surface that has never asked it. DEF-101's icon deliberately does NOT use TrayToolTip for this reason - its tip says 'MCP Router' and nothing more - so the fix for this row is also what lets the icon say something useful.
next: Feed AmbientSurfaceModel from the control API the Servers board already polls, then hand TrayToolTip to the icon. The witness is the same shape as the icon's: drive the router into a known state from outside the app and read the tip back - Shell_NotifyIconGetRect does not return the tip, so this one needs a UIA read of the flyout or the shell's own state readout instead.
resolution:
FIXED 2026-09-03. The ambient surface now renders a reading, and the reading comes from the router.

WHAT NOW READS THE ROUTER. MCPRouter.Shell.Model/Ambient/RouterStatusReader.cs polls the router's own GET /status over the loopback control port - ungated, so no token is read or sent - and AmbientStatusMapping turns that document into a reading: children[].inFlight summed is 'Serving tool calls', pendingAuth is 'Decisions waiting', neither is 'Router ready', and a body that cannot be parsed is 'Cannot reach router' rather than a quiet router. The endpoint is resolved per read through ControlEndpoint.BaseUrl(), the way the Servers board resolves it, so the surface follows the port the machine is actually configured for. ShellWindow polls it every two seconds and paints the pane footer, which is on screen whichever destination is selected; App holds one process-wide AmbientSurfaceModel so the pane and the notification-area tip cannot disagree, and NotificationAreaIcon.RefreshTooltip() carries a changed state into the tip through NIM_MODIFY.

THE DEFAULT IS THE FIX, AS MUCH AS THE READER IS. AmbientRouterState gained an Unknown member and it is FIRST, so default(AmbientRouterState) is 'nothing has read the router yet' and not AtRest. A model that has never been read cannot say 'Router ready'; it says 'Reading the router' / 'Nothing has read the router yet.', and its tray tip is the bare product name. The XAML literals 'Router ready' and 'All systems quiet' are gone from AmbientFlyoutView, which had them baked in as Text attributes.

TWO WORDINGS WERE CHANGED BECAUSE THEY NAMED THINGS NOTHING COUNTS. 'N items queued from your phone waiting for review' described a queue no code in this build reads; the surface counts the router's pendingAuth, so it now says 'N servers are waiting for you to sign in.' And the unreachable sentence named the literal 127.0.0.1:8879 whatever port the client had called; it now names the endpoint that was polled. Both are the same defect one layer down and are recorded here rather than folded into the green.

MEASURED FROM OUTSIDE THE APPLICATION. scripts/windows/uia/shell-lane.ps1 owns the router the shell is pointed at, and the arms stop it, put a stand-in on its port and start it again while the shell is never told anything; the pane is then read back off the automation plane. CASE-0470 ambient.routerStopped - the router is killed and the port confirmed silent, and the pane reads 'Cannot reach router' / 'The router daemon is not responding on 127.0.0.1:64947.' CASE-0471 ambient.workInFlight - a process outside the app answers /status with three calls in flight across two upstreams and the pane reads 'Serving tool calls' / '3 active tool calls in flight.', so the sum is the surface's. CASE-0472 ambient.signInWaiting - two upstreams in pendingAuth, and the pane reads 'Decisions waiting' / '2 servers are waiting for you to sign in.' CASE-0473 ambient.routerRunning - the product's own node router is started again and the pane reads 'Router ready', so the surface is not only reading the lane's stand-in. CASE-0474 ambient.silence - the router is taken away once more and the pane goes back to 'Cannot reach router', so its earlier readings were readings rather than a state it latched. CASE-0475 ambient.shellSurvivedRouterLoss - the shell was still on the automation plane after all of it.

WATCHED TO FAIL FIRST. A build with the model's default put back to AtRest and the poll never started - the defect exactly as filed - was run through the same lane on 2026-09-03: ambient.routerStopped, ambient.workInFlight, ambient.signInWaiting and ambient.silence all failed, each reporting the pane frozen at 'Router ready' / 'All systems quiet. No active calls or queued items.' while the router was stopped or answering something else. Transcript: planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/arming/def-301-planted-lane.txt. The unit arms were watched too: planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/arming/def-301-unit-plant.txt.

ONE ARM PASSED OVER THE PLANT AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH: ambient.routerRunning, because a surface frozen at 'Router ready' satisfies an arm that expects 'Router ready'. That is precisely why the other four exist, and why the first thing the section does is take the router away.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, kept here rather than folded into the green:
  - Nothing in this build mounts AmbientFlyoutView. It now renders from the model it is handed instead of from literals, but no operator can open it and no arm reads it. Filed as DEF-380.
  - The notification-area tip is refreshed through NIM_MODIFY and no instrument on this host reads a tooltip back: Shell_NotifyIconGetRect returns a rectangle and not the tip. The tip's content is therefore this application's own account of itself; the pane readout beside it is the part that is witnessed. Filed as DEF-380.
  - 'Work in flight' and 'a sign-in waiting' were driven with a stand-in on the router's port (scripts/windows/uia/router-status-stub.ps1) because neither can be induced in the real router on this host without a real upstream doing real work. The stand-in is what the app READ, not what recorded the effect, and the reachable/unreachable arms either side of it are against the product's own router.

title: The Cleanup board's Remove selected button reaches nothing and asks nothing
found: 2026-09-02, recorded while fixing DEF-102
evidence: CleanupBoard.OnRemoveSelectedClicked gets the selected rows and its body is the comment '// Removal dialog logic'. The rows themselves come from CleanupBoardModel.PopulateSampleData, so the board is offering to remove servers and skills that are not the operator's. Nothing on that board reads RequireConfirmationOnDestructive.
why-it-matters: DEF-102 landed the confirmation over the Servers board's removal and narrowed the switch's label to 'Confirm before removing a server'. This board carries a second destructive affordance that neither removes anything nor consults that setting, so a user who turned the setting on has not covered every Remove in the product - they have covered the one that works.
next: Point the board at the router's real server list, route its removal through ControlApiClient.RemoveServerAsync and the same setting the Servers board reads, and grow the lane an arm shaped like settings.requireConfirmation.effect over this board's button. Until then the button should say why it cannot act, the way the Reap idle button does.
resolution:
FIXED. Both halves of this row's `next` were taken, and the fallback it names was not needed.

THE ROWS ARE THE ROUTER'S. CleanupBoardModel.PopulateSampleData is DELETED, not bypassed. It invented five rows - pocketsmith, ai-elements, graphify, media-gen-pro, acceptance-e2e - and the board offered to remove them; a destructive control over rows that are not the operator's is worse than an inert one, because the inert one cannot act on the wrong thing. The only way a row reaches the model now is Adopt(ServersEnvelope, DateTimeOffset), which takes the router's own GET /servers answer: never-called is usage.calls == 0, quiet is usage.lastUsed older than the window. A board that got no answer has no rows and says so (Fail), because an empty list drawn silently over a router that never answered reads as 'nothing to propose'.

THE BUTTON REACHES THE ROUTER AND READS THE SETTING. OnRemoveSelectedClicked was the comment '// Removal dialog logic'. It now goes down the same path the Servers board's Remove does - ControlApiClient.RemoveServerAsync per selected row, gated by RequireConfirmationOnDestructive read at the moment of the press off the file the Settings board writes, not cached at construction. So an operator who turned that switch on has now covered both Removes in the product rather than the one that happened to work, which is what this row's why-it-matters asked for.

MEASURED AGAINST THE ROUTER, NOT THE DIALOG. Four arms in scripts/windows/uia/shell-lane.ps1 over two servers this lane declares for nothing else, lane-cleanup-gamma and lane-cleanup-delta (DEF-102's pair is already gone by the time these run):
  cleanup.requireConfirmation.baseline  the router lists both before anything is driven.
  cleanup.requireConfirmation.effect    setting On, Remove selected pressed, 'Keep it' pressed, and the ROUTER still lists gamma.
  cleanup.requireConfirmation.accepted  the same path with 'Remove permanently', and the router no longer lists it. A gate that can only refuse is not a gate.
  cleanup.requireConfirmation.silence   setting Off, no confirmation raised at all, and the router no longer lists delta. Without this the effect arm would pass identically over a board that always confirms and reads nothing.
The recorder is the router's own /servers listing read over the control API by the lane - a different process from the one that pressed the button, with no view of the dialog at all.

WATCHED TO FAIL, from both directions, transcripts in planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/arming/:
  cleanup-button-reaches-nothing-lane.txt   this defect replanted - the handler's body returned to the comment. effect, accepted and silence all went red ('a destructive button that asks nothing', 'the Cleanup board's button did nothing at all with the setting off'), while every settings.requireConfirmation arm stayed green, so the reds are about this board and not the harness.
  cleanup-dialog-is-a-decoration-lane.txt   the dialog raised unconditionally and its answer discarded. effect went red from the other side ('the dialog was a decoration over an operation that had already been decided') and silence went red ('turning it off removes no prompt').
cleanup.requireConfirmation.baseline HELD through both, so it is unarmed and says so.

CASE-0490..CASE-0493, REQ-090.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE:
  - SKILLS. CleanupKind.Skill is in the row vocabulary and this board now produces none. The router serves no skills route on this build (spec-WIN6 2.1; the Skills board's live reads answer 404), so 'this skill is unused' would be derived from no reading at all - the same defect wearing a different noun. The board says so on screen (CleanupBoardModel.SkillsNotEnumerated) rather than leaving the omission silent. Nothing is filed for it because the missing thing is a router route, not a client defect.
  - The per-row secondary button is GONE rather than wired. It carried 'Sign in instead', 'Keep' and 'Remove...' from the sample data and had no Click handler at all - three more affordances of exactly this row's shape, and nothing in this build implements any of the three verbs per row. The row's facts stay; the false affordance does not.
  - The quiet window is fixed at 30 days and the 'Unused for 30 days' selector reaches nothing. It is now disabled with its reason on the three channels the Reap idle button uses rather than left looking live, and the wiring is DEF-401.
  - The action row's false reassurance is DEF-400.

THE HEADLESS HALF, AND THE VACUOUS ASSERTION IT CAUGHT. MCPRouter.Shell.Tests.CleanupBoardModelTests is rewritten around Adopt(ServersEnvelope, DateTimeOffset) - every row in it is derived from the shape the router answers, because the defect these replace was a model that could produce rows with no router in the picture. Four plants were taken against the model and each was watched to red the arm named beside it:
  the selection intersect deleted           -> nothing went red, which is how the arm was found to be vacuous: the original test asserted only that a delisted server stops being counted, and it stops being counted because its row is gone either way. The test now adopts the server BACK and asserts the tick did not return, which is the case that matters - a tick held over a name the router had stopped listing re-arms itself the moment something with that name reappears. With the intersect deleted it reds.
  the selection cleared on every refresh    -> SelectionSurvivesARefresh and ASelectionTheRouterStoppedListingIsDropped
  the quiet window ignored (>= 1 day)       -> AServerJustInsideTheWindowIsNotACandidate and AdoptSortsServersIntoNeverCalledAndQuiet
  an unparseable lastUsed read as ancient   -> AServerWhoseLastUseIsUnreadableIsNotProposed
All four reverted.

ONE THING CHANGED THAT WAS NOT ASKED FOR, and the reason it was changed turned out to be wrong: the board no longer rebuilds its row tree on every poll - it compares a signature of what it would draw against what it drew and returns when they match. It was written after the shell died twice mid-sweep while the lane's out-of-process UIA client walked its tree, on the guess that a five-second teardown-and-rebuild behind a tree walk was the cause. THE GUESS DID NOT SURVIVE, and it was tested rather than argued: the shell died again with the guard in place at the FIRST destination, before the Cleanup board had ever been mounted, and then the whole of app/windows was stashed back to main's tree, rebuilt clean and run three more times - the UNMODIFIED shell died at `harnesses` on the first of those. So this is a pre-existing instability, not a regression from this change and not cured by it, and it is filed as DEF-402, and that row has since been closed: the cause was the lane itself, whose Start-Shell killed EVERY process named MCPRouter.Shell on the machine, so the other runner in this wave and this one were terminating each other's shell mid-sweep. Nothing had faulted, which is why there was never an unhandled-exception line or a Windows Error Reporting record. The kill is now scoped to the lane's own binary. The guard stays because it is right on its own merits: tearing down every element on a clock discards focus and any assistive client's handles whether or not the reading moved.

THE THIRD ARMING, AND THE STRONGEST ONE. The two plants above are reconstructions. The baseline runs taken to settle DEF-402 also drove these arms against the board AS COMMITTED ON MAIN - app/windows stashed to main's tree, rebuilt clean - and all three effect arms went red there: 'no row for lane-cleanup-gamma', because the board was drawing PopulateSampleData's five invented names and the router's own servers were not on it at all. Two consecutive runs, in planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/arming/cleanup-defect-as-committed-lane.txt. An arm that reds against the real defect in the real tree is a better reading than one that reds against a plant, because nobody chose what it was looking at.

title: The Cleanup board promised an undo that does not exist, under its destructive button

evidence: CleanupBoard.xaml's action row ended with the literal caption 'Removing is undoable for 30 days.', immediately beside the Remove selected button. Nothing in the Windows client, the control API or the router implements any undo: ControlApiClient.RemoveServerAsync sends DELETE /servers/{name}, and the router's DELETE branch drops the entry from servers.json and reloads. title: The shell lane kills every MCPRouter.Shell on the machine, so two runners in a wave terminate each other's shell mid-sweep
found: 2026-09-03, recorded while fixing DEF-302
evidence: CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED, 2026-09-03. shell-lane.ps1's Start-Shell stopped stale shells with `Get-Process 'MCPRouter.Shell'`, which names every process of that name on the MACHINE. Two runners in a fleet wave run this lane from two worktrees at once, so each one's Start-Shell terminated the other's shell partway through its sweep. The victim reported a destination CRASH at whichever destination it happened to be reading - which is why the four deaths landed on four different destinations, why none left an `unhandled:` line in shell-startup.log, and why none produced an Application Error or Windows Error Reporting event: nothing faulted, the process was killed. Four deaths in eleven runs on 2026-09-03, on BOTH trees - the DEF-302 branch and, after stashing app/windows back to main's and rebuilding clean, main's own. resolution:
FIXED by scoping the kill to this lane's own binary. Start-Shell now compares each candidate's Path against the lane's normalised ExePath and stops only what matches; two worktrees build to two absolute paths, so a lane can no longer reach another runner's shell. A process whose Path cannot be read - one running as another user - is LEFT ALONE and said out loud, because killing on a failed identity check is the behaviour being removed.

WATCHED TO FAIL, then to pass: scripts/windows/uia/foreign-shell-witness.ps1 puts a process named MCPRouter.Shell at a path that is not the lane's, runs the lane, and reads whether it survived.
  RED    against the committed lane, the stand-in was killed (exit 1) and the lane then reported NO VERDICT because its own shell never reached the plane - the failure mode in miniature. planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/arming/lane-kills-a-foreign-shell.txt
  GREEN  against the fix, the stand-in survived and the lane exited 0 - WHILE wd1's shell was live on the machine. planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/arming/lane-spares-a-foreign-shell.txt

TWO THINGS THE ARM ITSELF HAD TO LEARN, both recorded in its header because they are the difference between a reading and a green:
  A real second copy of the shell is the wrong stand-in. Started from an agent session it has no window station, draws nothing and often exits within seconds, and the arm reported NO VERDICT over a subject that died by itself. The stand-in is a renamed ping.exe: the lane's selection reads Name and Path and nothing else, so that is all the stand-in has to be.
  It must be started through an INTERACTIVE scheduled task. Started from session 0, Stop-Process from the lane's task in session 1 fails SILENTLY - the lane logged 'stopping a stale shell' three times against a process that outlived all three, and the arm passed while proving nothing. That near-miss is why the arm now also reads the lane's transcript: a stand-in that dies after this lane logged that it was LEAVING it was killed by something else, and the arm reports NO VERDICT rather than blaming this lane. It did exactly that once, on the run where wd1's lane - still carrying the machine-wide kill - took the stand-in.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: every other lane and script on this repository that stops a process by name. This fixes shell-lane.ps1 alone, and a runner on an older branch still kills machine-wide until it merges - which is why the green above was taken with another runner's shell live rather than on a quiet machine.
